    ISF · Kybliary community

    The community's documentary history

    From family recollections of spiritual beginnings around 1994–1995 and construction around 1996–1997 to state registration on 20 May 2005. Personal testimony and documentary sources are presented separately.

    Around 1994–1995

    Origins. The beginning of a spiritual journey

    Author of the historical account: Vitalii Mykolaiovych Ananchenko. Source: the community-supplied document “кибляры.docx”.

    This is Mykola Markovych Ananchenko’s personal religious testimony, conveyed in family recollections. Descriptions of a vision and healing reflect the narrators’ faith; they are not independently established medical or supernatural facts.

    The history of the Kybliary community begins around 1994–1995. An event in the life of Mykola Markovych Ananchenko profoundly changed his subsequent path and, as his family later understood it, marked the beginning of a wider spiritual story.

    In his own accounts, he experienced a state he called clinical death. He described a sense of being outside his body, seeing himself from the side and undergoing unusual spiritual experiences. The family account mentions about two hours; neither that duration nor the medical description is supported by medical records in the supplied material.

    According to his testimony, Jesus Christ appeared to him and asked:

    “Are you ready to leave everything: your wife, your children, your entire earthly life?”

    Mykola Markovych replied that he was ready.

    He then heard words that remained with him:

    “No, you are not ready yet. You still have much to do.”

    He described returning to his earthly life after this encounter.

    His family regards this event as the beginning of Mykola Markovych Ananchenko’s particular spiritual journey.

    Afterwards he became increasingly interested in Holy Scripture, reading and studying the Bible, reflecting on its texts and speaking with clergy. Prayer and spiritual searching gradually became central to his life.

    In time he began praying for people who approached him with life’s difficulties, illnesses and emotional distress. Mykola Markovych and some of those who visited believed he had received a particular gift of prayer and healing. This is their religious belief, rather than an independently established medical finding.

    At first this took place in an ordinary family home. There was no chapel, church or developed monastery grounds: only a home, prayer, Holy Scripture and people who gradually began to visit.

    Thus, in a small room in an ordinary house, amid everyday responsibilities and family life, the history of the spiritual centre that would become the Kybliary community began to unfold.

    The story that continued to grow began with prayer.

    Around 1996–1997

    First steps towards a house of mercy

    Over time, more people came to Mykola Markovych Ananchenko. Hearing about him, they arrived with illnesses, life’s difficulties and spiritual needs, asking for prayerful support.

    He was not yet a member of the clergy. He continued his own spiritual journey, prayed for people, studied Holy Scripture and supported those who approached him.

    Eventually the family home could no longer accommodate everyone. This was particularly difficult for visitors travelling from far away, who needed rest, meals and somewhere to stay as well as a place to pray.

    Growing needs called for a separate building where people could be welcomed, supported and offered temporary shelter.

    It was then that Mykola Markovych conceived the idea of building a house of mercy.

    According to the account, he approached the undertaking with responsibility and humility, seeking a blessing from a priest in Kybliary before putting the idea into practice.

    After receiving that blessing, he began taking practical steps.

    Around 1996–1997, a design for the future house of mercy was drawn up and approved. Construction then began with the laying of the foundation.

    An idea born of the need to help people gradually took physical shape.

    This was one of the first significant stages in the development of the future Kybliary community.

    Documentary history: registration on 20 May 2005 ↗

    The documentary history complements the family account of the community’s beginnings. Registration records support the legal dates below; these do not mark the beginning of the community’s spiritual life.

    ISF — In Search of the Fallen is the community’s approved brand and international presentation. It does not replace the full registered legal name, whose approved translation appears below.

    English translation of the Ukrainian registered name

    Religious Organization "Orthodox Religious Community of the Apostolic Tradition 'Search for the Fallen'"

    Translation of the Ukrainian registered name.

    12 March 2005

    General meeting of members

    Order No. 1, dated 20 May 2005, refers to Minutes No. 1 of a general meeting held on 12 March 2005. This is the earliest dated reference to an organisational decision in the supplied records. The minutes themselves were not supplied.

    Source: Order No. 1 of 20 May 2005

    20 May 2005

    State registration

    Certificate series A00 No. 386402 records the state registration of the religious organisation in Kybliary. The registration date is 20 May 2005 and the legal entity code is 33760792. The certificate names the Uzhhorod District State Administration of Zakarpattia Region as the registration authority.

    Source: State registration certificate

    20 May 2005

    Appointment of the head

    Order No. 1 appoints Vitalii Mykolaiovych Ananchenko as head of the religious organisation from 20 May 2005, with first-signature authority. This describes the appointment at that date; it does not establish the present administration.

    Source: Order No. 1 of 20 May 2005

    7 September 2005

    Dates in the register extract

    The extract's dates and entry-number field gives 20 May 2005, 7 September 2005 and entry No. 1 320 120 0000 000383. The September date should not replace the state registration date, which the certificate separately identifies as 20 May.

    Source: First page of the Unified State Register extract

    5 December 2013

    Register extract issued

    The extract's second page gives its issue date as 5 December 2013. It names Vitalii Mykolaiovych Ananchenko as head and records the main activity as 94.91, activities of religious organisations. These statements describe the extract at the time it was issued.

    Source: Second page of the Unified State Register extract

    The scope of the documentary account

    The registration dates are supported by the certificate below. The account of spiritual beginnings and construction comes from the family recollections of Vitalii Mykolaiovych Ananchenko. Approximate dates and personal religious experiences are not independently established medical or archival findings.
